### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a83032b1d2eef2ffbd53003bfef065f1af2127c0` — the merge of head `ae6b35c1632000f5cdd3a4146960ce339b76c0de` into base `5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a83032b1d2eef2ffbd53003bfef065f1af2127c0 && git checkout a83032b1d2eef2ffbd53003bfef065f1af2127c0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812 ae6b35c1632000f5cdd3a4146960ce339b76c0de && git checkout -B drift-repro 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812 && git merge --no-ff ae6b35c1632000f5cdd3a4146960ce339b76c0de

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ae6b35c1632000f5cdd3a4146960ce339b76c0de`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23297 (body and all five comments: triage `6149701838`, unlock `6149850778`, the claim `6160266617` as amended in place, the os-dev-report `6162849757`, the seat ACCEPT `6162928143`); PR #23408 (body, nine-file list, net diff against `main` at the head: +533 / -58); the 40 check-runs on the head; committed source read with `git show` / `git grep` against `origin/claude/issue-23297-package-axis-delete-draft` and `origin/main` (merge base `e4ec6ec1a`). Nothing built, run, re-run or ablated.

**Check-runs on the head, as found (40, all `completed`; 0 failure, 0 in progress).** The five required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates` success · `TypeScript Type Check` success · `Test Core` success (shards 1/6 to 6/6 each success) · `Build Core` success · `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success. The rest, success: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, filter. Skipped by path filter (9): Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL).

### ① Derived judgments

**Item 1 — the registry heal after a per-package delete (a widening of what the registry-backed and data doors serve after such a delete): RIGHT.**
- Order in `deleteMetaItem` on the head: `repo.delete` (the repository removes the row physically with `engine.delete('sys_metadata', …)`), then `restoreArtifactRegistryView`, then `shouldDropStorage` / `dropObjectStorage`. The new tier (protocol.ts 20395 to 20477) reads `sys_metadata` at `type: canonical, name, state: 'active', organization_id: null` plus the bundle-member predicate. The deleted row is gone and a draft row is not `active`, so the tier can re-register only rows still stored; the method returns at its top for any organization-scoped delete, so only an env-wide delete reaches it. It never resurrects the deleted item: the CONTROL pin (both rows deleted: `getObject` and `getItem` undefined, data CRUD `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` 404) is in the diff and was green before and after the fix per the dev's before-leg.
- "Only what is stored, as a boot registers it": the rows go through `applyRegistryWriteThrough` under `canonicalMetaType`, built with `convertStoredItem` and `storedRowDocument`, with the sealed-object skip spelled `canonical === 'object' && isUnservedSealedOverlay` — the same object-only skip the boot loop applies (`loadMetaFromDb`: `if (normalizedType === 'object') continue;`). `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry`'s own guards still apply on this path (an organization-scoped row is not registered; a bound view another package ships is declined, #22057), and on a kernel whose registry does not take stored rows the non-object write-through registers nothing and the tier returns without retiring — the entry was never there on such a kernel, so nothing moves. A read failure stops the walk through `rethrowUnlessMetadataStoreUnprovisioned`; an unprovisioned store reads as no row.
- The stale-owner unregister: the limb runs only for `canonical === 'object' && !isArtifactBacked(canonical, name)`; `isArtifactBacked` answers from the artifact-only lookup (a genuine code package `_packageId`, the `'sys_metadata'` sentinel excluded), so a code-shipped object is never unregistered here. `bindings` keys a package-less row as `'sys_metadata'`, the sentinel `classifyObjectContribution` registers a package-less runtime owner under, so a package-less remaining row keeps a package-less owner and only an owner outside the remaining bindings is removed. `registry.unregisterObject` throws on foreign extenders; the catch warns and returns with nothing retired, the tier-3 limb's own disposition. Rows are then re-registered in the store's return order, the order a boot reads them in, and `registerObject` keeps one owner per name as it does at boot.
- The side effect the PR body declares (a read naming the deleted package now falls through to the registry entry and serves the remaining row) follows from one owner per name; declared in the acceptance notes, acceptable.
- The two existing pins that moved: the write-through call-site count is 7 on the head (counted), the seventh being this tier, traced in the pin's header; the view-container fixture now removes the active row before calling the heal directly, which is the real call order, a fixture correction and not a weakened assertion.

**Item 2 — a package-less draft save of an item two or more packages hold is refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with the `?package=` remedy; a one-package item still inherits: RIGHT.**
- `resolveWriteHead` (repository 814 to 876) reads every active row with the same `activeWhere` the old single-row read used (two-scope reach for an organization-scoped repository, env-wide otherwise), collects non-empty string `package_id` values (the same test the old code applied to the one row it read, so a package-less row beside a package's is not a binding), inherits on exactly one binding, and on two or more leaves `targetPackageId` null and reports `ambiguousPackages` sorted. `put` throws `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal('save', …)` immediately after that resolution inside `withTxn`, ahead of the optimistic lock, the no-op check and every insert, update and history write: nothing is written (pinned: row count and history length unchanged, both storage orders, door and repository). `headAt` ignores `ambiguousPackages` and answers the package-unbound draft key with `packageId: null` (pinned both orders). The one-package control with a package-less active row beside it is pinned in both storage orders at the door and the repository; naming one package saves that package's draft (pinned).
- The move of `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal` into `sys-metadata-repository.ts` keeps its words: I diffed the function on `main` (protocol.ts 1181 to 1223) against the head (repository 567 to 588) — identical apart from indentation and the `export` keyword, the verb-keyed `'save'` / `'delete'` sentences included. protocol.ts imports it and its two call sites (the direct save at 21769, the delete at 28476) are unchanged. `index.ts` exports a named list from that module (`SysMetadataRepository`, `resetEnvWritableMetadataTypes` and five types) and `package.json` exposes only the `.` entry, so the function reaches no public entry: no public-surface change.
- One scoping difference, checked and judged acceptable: the direct save's `packagelessAddress` reads env-wide rows only, while the draft inheritance keeps its #11087 two-scope reach. For an env-wide caller the two doors read the same rows and answer the same refusal. For an organization-scoped caller the draft door now counts the organization's own bound row as a binding; that row was already one the old `findOne` could return, so the change is from a storage-order pick to a refusal, with no new row brought into scope — the narrowing the card asked for.

**Item 3 — the delete's lock gate hands the named package to `getEffectiveLock`; the dev's measurement that the verdict is unchanged and only the refusal prose moves: UPHELD.**
- `assertLockAllowsDelete` now makes the call `lockWriteRefusal` (the save gate) has made since #21761: `getEffectiveLock(type, name, packageId)`. In `getEffectiveLock` the package reaches `artifactLockLayerAt` and `readLockGateOverlayLayer`. The artifact set is `shippedArtifactsOf` (the package-less lookup plus every shipping package's own artifact, the single owner for an object) and the overlay rows are read with no package predicate (`overlayLockLayerAt`: `type, name, state 'active', organization_id null`); neither reader is in this diff and neither narrows its set by the address. The address reaches only the two selections, and that they bind the strictest lock whatever package the request names is already pinned on `main` on the real `SchemaRegistry` (#21803 cases 1 to 3: a save naming A refused `full` when only B ships it, both orders; the package-less row's `no-overlay` binding a request naming A). The delete's verdict under the save gate's call is therefore the save's verdict. The new case 4 pins `remove` equal to `save` (code, status, lock, lockReason) with both reads reporting `deletable: false`; case 5 pins the prose moving to the named package's reason, red before the fix (2 red, delete naming B under both orders, per the dev's ablation and before-leg).
- The card's "Wanted" pin for item 3 (`?package=P` allowed when only Q's copy is locked) is deliberately not delivered, and that is right: delivering it would reverse #21761 / #21803 and make the delete door looser than both reads naming P. The question goes to ③.
- The delete spreads `packageId` only when truthy; an empty string reads as none, consistent with `boundPackageOf` and `shippingPackagesOf`.

**Negative controls:** item 1, the heal tier off: 5 red, CONTROL green; item 2, `put`'s refusal off: 4 red; item 3, the package dropped from the gate call: 2 red. Each is the pin that fails without its fix, as the claim required.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, a `**BREAKING**` banner, title `fix(metadata-protocol)!:`. The package publishes (no `private` flag; `18.0.0-next.0`), and it is the only published package whose source moves — the two `packages/objectql` files are tests. `minor` for a breaking change is the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces, and its level axis (a `yes` declaration must grade at least one moved published package `minor` or above) is met. `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head.
- **ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right for this diff.** No authorable spelling, Zod schema, stored row or exported declaration moves: the moved function is not on the package entry, `assertLockAllowsDelete` and `resolveWriteHead` are private, and `deleteMetaItem`'s request already carried `packageId`. What narrows is a runtime write door whose remedy is a request parameter, nothing `objectstack migrate meta` could rewrite; what widens is the registry after a delete. The gate's refusal condition (a migration prescription in the changeset body) does not fire: the FROM / TO paragraphs describe door behaviour, not a code rewrite. The sibling precedent on `main`, `.changeset/23165-direct-save-resolves-package.md`, carries the same level, the same arm and the same disposition for the same door family.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: right.** `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines that arm as a diff that widens one surface and narrows another, both facts read. Item 1 widens (the registry-backed and data doors serve a remaining row after a per-package delete where they answered 404), item 2 narrows (`200` to `409` on the draft door), item 3 admits nothing. The claim as amended in place at ACCEPT, PR body line 2 and the changeset carry the same spelling; PR body line 1 is `Fixes #23297` with no other closing keyword beside a card number.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviations (six), each answered or informational:**
1. `Clause-②` read `yes` in the claim and `yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and changeset: answered — the seat amended the claim in place; all three carriers now agree (verified above).
2. File surface beyond the claim's regions (the import line, the moved refusal, one docblock line in `packagelessAddress`; two existing pins; two `objectql` test files): answered — the seat amended the claim; the nine-file list matches the amended surface, the three protocol.ts extras are exactly those hunks, the `objectql` files are tests only.
3. One local test run killed by the dev's own timeout wrapper and discarded, then re-run: informational — the head's `Test Core` fold and its six shards concluded success.
4. `check:type-check-debt` exit 124 at `a77f32b92`, exit 0 at the head: answered by `Type Check · debt ledger` success on the head.
5. The dropStorage probe ran with a stale cli dist: informational — metadata-protocol, objectql and spec dist were rebuilt, which is the path the measured behaviour takes; the result is filed as #23415.
6. Model-free commit trailers: consistent with the AGENTS.md commit-message rule.

**`open_questions` item 3 (A: keep the ruled lock rule; B: a package-addressed lock), answered A by the seat with no follow-up card: inside the card's triage direction.** Triage's direction for item 3 reads, verbatim in effect, "hands `packageId` through to `getEffectiveLock`, at the save gate's parity" — which is what shipped. Triage's lane reasoning (that parity admits a request the door refuses today) was the card's premise, now measured false; the lane consequence (`Clause-②: yes`, contract-tier review) still holds through item 1, so nothing in the grade or lane turns on it. B would reverse #21803, a ruling of weeks ago, and restate ADR-0010 §3.3's one-answer lock per package, on the doors and the reads together — a new decision, not this card's to take, and the dev measured zero item locks declared in `examples/` at the head. A keeps door and reads in lockstep; not filing B without a named need is right.

**Out-of-scope findings, filed by the seat as #23415 and #23416 — neither is a defect this diff makes false or owns:**
- **#23415** (`dropStorage=true` on a per-package delete drops the table while another package's row remains): a separate card is right. The root is `shouldDropStorage` (protocol.ts 20733), which asks only type, state and the `sys_` prefix and never whether a row remains; this diff does not touch it. Noted for the fixer: on this head the heal runs before the drop, so the scenario now leaves the remaining package's object registered over a dropped table (`500 DATABASE_ERROR`), where `main` left it retired (`404`); the data loss is identical and pre-exists. The registration is correct given the row remains, and both remedies the dev names (refuse the delete, or skip the drop and say so) leave this heal right. #23415 was measured on this head's tree, so its symptom text is already the post-PR shape.
- **#23416** (a second package's save of a runtime-authored object answers `200` while `registerObject` refuses the ownership): a separate card is right. `classifyObjectContribution` asks only `getPackagedObjectOwner`; untouched here. This diff's object limb is written for exactly the state #23416 describes (the second row stored but unregistered, the owner the first package) and heals it after a delete; it does not change the save. Noted for the fixer: the new heal pin's `twoPackageObject` fixture builds that state through `saveMetaItem` with `console.warn` mocked, so a fix that refuses the second save must seed the rows directly — a fixture change, not a weakened pin.

**The two "carrier: none" observations** (rollback, restore and the raw-engine delete read the active row with no package predicate; the package-less draft receipt does not name the inherited package) are read from source, not measured; the seat placed them in the acceptance notes, which is Prime Directive 10's disposition for a note that is not yet a filed defect.

**Landing class:** none of the nine paths is on the governed register (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success); 591 changed lines; head repository equals base repository; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft, base `main`.
